messages:
Matt: hey team — opened PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4821. Small runtime change: compact KV batching + change default TTL from 30s -> 60s for cold prefix entries. needs a quick review before merging today

ci-bot: PR 4821 — build started, running unit tests and integration smoke.

Sylvia: PTAL in ~30m, i'm deep in another review but can do a quick pass after lunch :thumbsup:

Oliver: quick skim — the compaction logic looks fine, one minor question about the TTL units. can you show the diff for the config patch?

Matt: sure — snippet below. main change is in kv_cache/config.py and the batcher behavior to trigger compaction earlier for low-memory hosts.

```
# kv_cache/config.py
DEFAULT_TTL_SEC = 60  # was 30
COMPACT_THRESHOLD = 0.6  # fraction of storage used to trigger compaction
```

Matt: also tweaked batcher loop to compact after N idle batches instead of time-based to reduce prewarm races observed on small GPUs.

Rachael: CI shows a flaky test in python/integration/test_prefetch.py (timeout). looks unrelated but worth rerunning after addressing comments.

ci-bot: PR 4821 — unit tests: passed, integration: failed (1 flaky test).

Oliver: noted. My comment: in kv_cache/evict.py you call `.expire()` with seconds but DEFAULT_TTL_SEC is an int. consider using explicit timedelta for clarity. otherwise LGTM. left inline comment.

Matt: good catch — i'll update to use datetime.timedelta to avoid confusion. pushing patch now.

Matt: pushed a fix, retriggering CI.

ci-bot: PR 4821 — re-run started.

Sylvia: i can verify the batcher change against our perf harness later today. if it doesn't regress tail latency we can merge.

Nate: if CI is green and sylvia gives a quick thumbs we'll merge in the 10:00-10:30 PST window and watch canary. i'll own the rollout.

ci-bot: PR 4821 — all checks passed.

Rachael: ran a quick local smoke with small-GPU config, compaction triggered as expected, no obvious stalls. :+1:

Sylvia: LGTM from perf side, no increase in 95th on my harness.

Oliver: approved.

Matt: great — thanks all. Nate — merging now and starting canary. will monitor logs for prewarm races.

Nate: got it. keeping an eye on metrics and will rollback if any error spikes. :eyes:

Matt: thanks :shipit:

Rachael: thanks!
